name: Bank of India
title: Bank of India - 532149 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Bank of India guides FY27 advances 15-16% and deposits 16-17%, ROA above 1% by March 2027, and CASA ratio slipped to 34.16%; ECL front-loading from Q3 is the key unquantified risk.

summary.headline: Bank of India Q2 FY27: H1 net profit about Rs 6,000 crore, Global NIM 2.47%, Gross NPA 1.60%; ECL front-loading planned from Q3, about 0.5% CRAR impact per year.
summary.overview: Management reported strong YoY growth: global business up 21.13% to Rs 18.92 lakh crore, and global advances up 20.58%. Operating profit rose 33.18% to Rs 5,089 crore and net profit rose 25.32% to Rs 3,202 crore for Sept'26 (the Q2 figure as stated on the call). Asset quality improved, with Gross NPA at 1.60% and Net NPA at 0.42%, and credit cost fell to 0.12% from 0.15% in June'26. Global NIM eased 5 bps YoY to 2.47%, which management attributed mainly to FCNR-linked leverage. Management guided FY27 global advances growth of 15-16% and global deposit growth of 16-17%, and said ECL provisioning will begin from Q3 after Board approval.

financial_highlights.change: +Rs 20,539 crore YoY; ratio down from prior quarters
down 5 bps from 2.52% (management cited Sept'25 at 2.41%)

segments.name: Corporate and pipeline
segments.commentary: Corporate pipeline about Rs 65,000 crore as of 30 Sept; total pipeline across corporate, RAM, digital, pool/co-lending and supply chain about Rs 86,000-87,000 crore. Largest sector pipelines are renewable energy (over Rs 12,000 crore), power (over Rs 9,000 crore) and roads (over Rs 5,000 crore).

segments.name: RAM
segments.commentary: RAM advances up 18.68% YoY to Rs 4.13 lakh crore, 58.63% of gross advances, with RAM pipeline about Rs 20,000 crore.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Gold loan book about Rs 61,000 crore, mostly agriculture with some MSME and retail; gold loan NPA about 0.13%, LTV capped at 75%.

segments.name: Overseas book
segments.commentary: Overseas advances up 35.21% YoY to Rs 1.51 lakh crore against overseas deposits up 11.52% to Rs 1.37 lakh crore; FCNR raise of USD 2.2 billion was deployed into the international loan book.

segments.name: Supply chain / trade
segments.commentary: Supply chain book just over Rs 1,000 crore, with a Rs 1,500 crore first-year target; trade and MSME-linked assets grew about 10% in the quarter.

guidance_outlook: FY27 global advances growth guided at 15-16% and global deposit growth at 16-17%.
ROA guided above 1% on a quarterly basis; management said ROA was above 1% in March'26, June'26 and Sept'26, and expects above 1% in March'27. FY28 expected to be better.

ECL: provisions expected to start from Q3 FY27 after Board approval, with Q3 and Q4 as front-loading quarters; ECL regime applies from 1 April 2027. Ballpark CRAR impact about 0.5% per year over the next 4 years.
NIM expected to gain about 6-7 bps from the 25 bps repo hike, with deposit repricing staggered because about 60% of term deposits mature in 1 to 18 months.
Recovery in written-off accounts expected to sustain the run rate of about Rs 900-1,000 crore a quarter; non-interest income expected to hold above Rs 2,500 crore a quarter.
capex_capacity: Technology budget for opex and capex (core IT, digital, cybersecurity) said to be unchanged for FY27; Big Four consultants engaged on IT, digital and cybersecurity transformation.
AI policy approved by the Board; current AI use is predictive (Data Lake project), with analytics-led leads above Rs 21,000 crore.
Centralised supply chain branch in Mumbai handles pool, co-lending, trades and supply chain; 69 zones each asked to onboard one new supply chain vendor per month.
ECL: consultant onboarded; computation covers PD, LGD and SICR; Board note to be presented, with clarity expected by Q3.
demand_pricing: Domestic deposit and advances growth remained strong YoY, with management saying no impact from the macro headwinds is foreseen on FY27 business growth.
66% of domestic advances are repo-linked; the bank passed on the 25 bps repo hike on the day of the ALCO meeting.
Management said that about 7% of the retail portfolio is unsecured.
Infra: outstanding roughly flat YoY despite sanctions; some COD projects refinanced by other lenders at low rates, leading to churn; full disbursement takes 7-8 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How large is the ECL provisioning need, how much is already provided, and what is the road ahead?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the broad total will not be shared until the Board note; the CRAR impact is about 0.5% per year over 4 years, covered by profits (H1 profit above Rs 6,000 crore, run rate of about Rs 12,000 crore for FY27). No ECL provision has been made yet; front-loading expected from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Will the bank still meet its growth targets given global and drought headwinds?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it sees no impact on FY27 business growth at present, citing a pipeline of about 10% of the loan book, GST collections above Rs 2 lakh crore a month and e-way bills of Rs 13-14 crore a month.

qa_highlights.question: How much can NIM improve from the rate hike, and how will CASA be raised?
qa_highlights.answer: The FCNR raise cost about 5 bps of NIM. The repo hike is expected to add 6-7 bps, with a lag on deposits. Bulk deposits are being used to fund credit growth, while retail term deposits are about 43% of total deposits.

qa_highlights.question: What drove non-interest income, and why is other income down?
qa_highlights.answer: Recoveries from written-off accounts rose about 190% YoY to Rs 978 crore, and treasury/forex profit rose 157% to Rs 411 crore. Non-interest income was Rs 2,700 crore, up 25% YoY.

qa_highlights.question: Is there stress in the gold loan book after NBFC concerns?
qa_highlights.answer: Gold loan NPA is about 0.13%. Management said the SOP calls for two notices before auction, the CBS system monitors LTV, and the LTV is capped at 75%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the government stake and any capital raise plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Promoter holding is 73.8%, within the 75% SEBI limit. No government indication to reduce stake further and no capital raise plan.

risks_watch: ECL transition from 1 April 2027: quantum of front-loading and CRAR impact, pending Board approval and the Q3 update.
NIM pressure from the FCNR leverage and falling CASA ratio (34.16%); pace of deposit repricing after the repo hike.
Dependence on lumpy recoveries from written-off accounts for non-interest income; 2-3 large accounts drove the quarter.
Macro risks: West Asia crisis, crude prices, drought and El Nino effects in parts of Maharashtra, and possible further RBI rate hikes.
Overseas advances growing 35% YoY against 11.5% overseas deposit growth, which lifts reliance on FCNR funding.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, asset quality and profitability, with management stressing the strength of its systems. It was more cautious and deflecting on ECL quantum, CASA ratio and macro risks, and gave no number on the total ECL requirement.
key_quotes: So, ECL impact, we have already started doing the computation and other kinds of things, whether it is the PD, whether it is the LGD, SICR, and other kinds of things.
So, we expect that from Q3 onwards we will be making the provisions.
At present, we do not see any impact which may have on our business growth numbers for this financial year.

growth.why: FY27 global advances guided at 15-16% and deposits at 16-17%, backed by a Rs 65,000 crore corporate pipeline (total pipeline ~Rs 86,000-87,000 crore) and a 25 bps repo hike passed through, but no specific capacity or contracted order numbers were given.
